## Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Training-pair margins cannot explain why broad matches outrank precise ones. Rank-based probes improve comparability but remain candidate-dependent. (2) Feedback implicates recent, repeated evidence. Neither recurrence nor textual similarity establishes intent, compatibility, or satisfied demand. (3) The compatibility view supports inexpensive interventions. Correct attribution nevertheless requires explicit prefix construction, positional handling, and identifiable users.

**Related work.** (1) CETRec separates temporal effects; sequence-pattern research identifies availability confounding. Shuffling preserves item multisets but does not eliminate this confounding. (2) Semantically Consistent Contrastive Learning and ROAR motivate caution about perturbation-induced distribution shift. Explanation faithfulness does not establish that a proposed architecture change will help. (3) Sampling-reliability research establishes candidate dependence, while adaptive-holdout research warns against repeated validation selection. Fixed panels improve reproducibility without preventing selection overfitting.

## Framework and directions

| Direction | Observable evidence | Intervention | Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Temporal dependence | Positions; available timestamps | Recent removal; older-context shuffle | Position differs from elapsed time |
| Repeated interests | Recurring IDs; lexical similarity | Remove supporting events | Deduplication can eliminate recurrence; similarity is a proxy |
| Specific usefulness | Explicit title/description attributes | Audit supported attribute conflicts | Unknown compatibility requires abstention |
| Ranking reliability | Fixed candidate scores | Target rank; pairwise wins; top-10 overlap | Sampled ranking differs from full-catalog ranking |

## Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each dimension has a positive (+) and negative (−) assessment.

1. **Paired perturbation diagnosis — 5/7/5.** Originality: + integrates controlled probes; − established attribution methods. Potential: + prioritizes ablations; − prescription validity remains unproven. Difficulty: + reuses scoring hooks; − identity, padding, positions, and controls require care. References: CETRec, ACCENT, ROAR.
2. **Recent-history residual scorer — 4/7/4.** Add a weighted recent-embedding mean to SASRec’s final representation. Originality: + targeted combination; − familiar recency modeling. Potential: + inexpensive adaptation; − can amplify incidental purchases. Difficulty: + small scoring change; − requires retraining and matching predictor changes. Reference: CETRec.
3. **Evidence-filtered lexical negatives — 6/6/6.** Mix random negatives with lexical neighbors exhibiting explicit attribute conflicts. Originality: + links attributes and conservative sampling; − hard-negative mining is established. Potential: + targets broad-relatedness errors; − conflicting attributes need not imply irrelevance. Difficulty: + TF-IDF needs no pretrained weights; − reliable conflict extraction is demanding. Reference: Hard-BPR.

## Selected idea: paired perturbation diagnosis

At 0% progress, retain diagnosis as the first experiment, with reduced potential and increased difficulty ratings. Its contribution is a reproducible test of model dependence; beneficial architecture prescriptions require separate retraining evidence.

Freeze an identified training-user panel, prefixes, candidate sets, strengths, controls, and metrics before search. Obtain identities from `view.user_train` or an explicit sidecar: loader tuples contain none. For loader position `t`, use only `sequence[:t+1]` and `positive[t]`; never expose later events.

```text
for identified prefix, target in frozen_panel:
    candidates = fixed_candidates(prefix, target)
    baseline = rank(right_align(prefix), candidates)
    for eligible intervention:
        measure rank_change, pairwise_wins, top10_overlap
        compare repeated matched controls; record coverage
aggregate prefixes within users, then within categories
```

Separate recent removal, repeated-support removal, and older-context shuffling. Measure recurrence coverage first; zero eligibility means unavailable evidence. Compare deletion/repacking with position-preserving masking where supported. Analyze overlapping removal sets separately, exclude empty histories, and report distribution-shift limitations.

Preserve `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)`, return schema, actual-model evaluation, and state restoration. Empty results return null with counts. Predefine a small ablation set and directional predictions; retain every trial and match training budgets and checkpoint rules. Only the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10 selects models. Diagnostic effects and descriptive paired uncertainty cannot establish causal preferences or full-catalog quality.

idea.description: Extend the compatibility-preserving diagnostic adapter with reproducible, identified-user sequence interventions, fixed-candidate target ranks, pairwise win rates, and top-10 overlap. Separate recency, observable repeated-interest support, older-context order, and positional artifacts; prospectively test whether diagnostic predictions anticipate improvements from a small predefined set of trained interventions.
idea.motivation: Existing embedding geometry and raw margins cannot resolve the reported mismatch between broad relatedness and specific recent interests. Early-stage research benefits from inexpensive mechanism checks before substantial training expenditure, but inference-time sensitivity alone cannot justify model changes. The revised design retains the diagnostic-first direction while explicitly testing its usefulness for choosing subsequent experiments.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Inspect the actual view.model and use the adapter's log2feats and predict_score so its trained scoring head remains intact. Save model.training, evaluate under no_grad, and restore the original state in finally. Preserve existing valid probes, remove unsupported metadata-category breakdowns, and report null plus eligible counts for undefined statistics.

Freeze a bounded deterministic training-user panel before model search, using category and stable user IDs from view.user_train or an explicit diagnostic sidecar. The loader tuple (None, sequence, positive, negative) cannot identify users; never infer identity from shuffled batch indices or matching histories. Prefer directly constructing examples from ordered training histories: for an observed history h and predefined transition j, use h[:j] as history and h[j] as target. Specify a cap, such as five most recent eligible transitions per selected user, and preserve the resulting manifest across trials. If extracting loader examples, accept only positions with nonzero sequence[b,t] and positive[b,t], and use sequence[b,:t+1] with positive[b,t] as target. Example: [0,a,b,c] with positives [0,b,c,d] yields [a]→b, [a,b]→c, [a,b,c]→d. Never append the target or later sequence entries. Record truncation to the model's maximum length.

For independent-prefix diagnosis, right-align nonpadding prefix items in a zero-padded length-L tensor and recompute the unperturbed baseline. Score the greatest nonzero position, which is L−1 for nonempty right-aligned prefixes; nonzero_count−1 is incorrect for left padding. Verify the actual encoder's causal and padding masks. Independent right-aligned scores need not equal original training-position scores because absolute positional embeddings change. If attributing an exact training-position prediction, preserve its original positions, clear its suffix, and score feature t; label this as a distinct protocol.

Construct a deterministic candidate set per identified example containing its target and up to 99 distinct nonpadding catalog negatives, excluding the user's known training-history items and target. When the target occurs in training history, retain it explicitly as the positive exception. Do not inspect held-out histories for exclusions. Use seed 42 with a stable manifest-defined per-example seed, sample without replacement, and record actual candidate counts for small catalogs. Reuse candidates across interventions, controls, and model comparisons. These training-prefix candidate sets are diagnostic sets, not the host's validation candidates. Include the loader-paired negative as an optional separately labeled comparison, without mixing its interpretation with the fixed-set results.

Define target rank as one plus the number of candidates with greater score, plus equal-score candidates with smaller item ID. Define pairwise win rate against negatives using the same deterministic ordering. Define top-10 overlap as intersection size divided by min(10, candidate_count). Report perturbed-minus-baseline rank, perturbed-minus-baseline pairwise win rate, overlap, candidate counts, intervention size, retained length, removal fraction, and control variability. Positive rank change means worse target ranking. Strictly increasing score transformations preserve these statistics subject to numerical ties.

Use predefined removal strengths, for example k=max(1,floor(0.2*n)), only when at least one event remains. Recent removal deletes the latest k events. Older-context shuffling permutes observed events except the latest, preserves the item multiset and padding pattern, and requires at least two older events. Define exact repeated support from item IDs occurring at least twice in the observed prefix, without consulting the target. Measure per-category repeat-user coverage and repeated-event counts first: preprocessing may eliminate exact repeats, but do not assume the pinned pipeline does so. Zero eligible users means unavailable evidence. An optional semantic-support variant must separately specify train-catalog TF-IDF word/character features, normalization, similarity threshold, clustering rule, and coverage before use; it is a lexical proxy, not an intent label.

For each deletion, use a predefined number of deterministic random control draws, such as ten, matched on removal count and original history length. Match coarse recency/popularity strata and contiguous-block structure where feasible; compute popularity from training interactions only. Report failed matches, duplicate control masks, and the number of distinct alternatives. Exact recency matching for latest-block removal can leave no distinct control; mark the content-versus-position contrast unidentified rather than silently weakening matching. Analyze targeted effects and targeted-minus-control effects separately. For overlapping recent and repeated-support sets, evaluate the sets, their intersection, exclusive portions, and union when eligible; never add their effects.

Deletion/repacking changes surviving absolute positions. Where the actual architecture exposes explicit position IDs and correctly supports internal masking, add a position-preserving intervention that retains surviving items' original position IDs and masks removed tokens. Use the identical scoring head, verify masks, and score the final surviving query. Do not assume zeroing an internal token is safe in every SASRec implementation. If unsupported, report the positional contrast as unavailable. Neither masking nor repacking is artifact-free; stratify by retained length and removal fraction, exclude empty histories, and treat plausible same-length replacements as optional, separately specified sensitivity analyses.

Aggregate eligible prefix effects within identified users before category summaries, reporting user and prefix coverage separately for each intervention. Macro summaries use equal category weights only where all four category statistics are defined; otherwise report category results and explicitly mark the four-category summary unavailable. For feedback from five users per category, retain individual counts and distinguish immediate choice, plausible later, explicit rejection, and unassessable responses; do not fabricate labels or infer population acceptance from this small panel.

To test prescription value, preregister a small set of trained changes, their directional predictions, matched controls, compute allocation, and checkpoint rules. Include an unchanged baseline and a recency-residual ablation, updating its predictor writer and checkpoint loading if implemented. Compare each model through the unchanged host validation protocol, preserving splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, evaluation seed 42, and all four routes. If per-user validation outcomes are supplied, use paired within-category user bootstrap resampling with equal category weights; label intervals after selection as descriptive and conditional on fixed candidates. Otherwise do not invent uncertainty estimates. With 200 users per category, one changed hit moves category HR@10 by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR@10 by 0.125 points. Cap comparisons and retain every trial because repeated validation reuse can overfit.

Batch and cap diagnostic examples to limit GPU cost; training, diagnostics, debugging, and failed trials all share the 43,200 GPU-second budget. Remain single-GPU. Keep DATA_DIR as os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preserve dataset routing, use the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200, and write manifests and artifacts beneath the trial directory. No architecture or predictor change is required for the diagnostic-only adapter. No hidden test access, split changes, external datasets, pretrained downloads, unavailable review fields, or inferred simulator traits are permitted. Complete host rankings remain required even when diagnostic judgments abstain.
idea.pseudocode:
panel = freeze_identified_training_examples(view.user_train, seed=42)
# Save category, user_id, transition, prefix, target, candidates, and control masks.
saved_training_state = view.model.training
view.model.eval()
try:
  with no_grad():
    for example in bounded(panel):
      prefix, target = example.prefix, example.target
      assert target_is_next_observed_event_without_suffix_leakage(example)
      candidates = example.fixed_candidates
      baseline = score_adapter(right_align(prefix), candidates, final_nonpadding=True)
      interventions = eligible_recent_repeat_and_older_shuffle(prefix)
      for intervention in interventions:
        if intervention.leaves_empty_history:
          record_ineligible(example, intervention)
          continue
        changed = apply_repacking_protocol(prefix, intervention)
        scores = score_adapter(changed, candidates, final_nonpadding=True)
        record_rank_delta_win_delta_overlap(baseline, scores)
        record_coverage_sizes_and_retained_length()
        if intervention.is_deletion:
          controls = example.predefined_distinct_matched_controls(intervention)
          record_matching_coverage_and_unidentified_contrasts(controls)
          for control in controls:
            record_control_effect(score_adapter(control, candidates), baseline)
          if architecture_supports_explicit_positions_and_internal_masks:
            record_position_preserving_effect(prefix, intervention, candidates)
          else:
            record_unavailable_position_contrast()
    results = aggregate_prefixes_within_users_then_categories()
    return {'metrics': results, 'metric_definitions': explicit_definitions}
finally:
  view.model.train(saved_training_state)

# Separate, budgeted experiment; diagnostic effects are not validation scores.
freeze_ablation_predictions_controls_budgets_and_checkpoint_rules()
for predefined_model_change in capped_ablation_set:
  train_with_pinned_splits_and_seeds()
  update_predictor_writer_if_scoring_changes()
  retain_trial_and_obtain_unchanged_host_validation_HR10()
compare_predictions_with_observed_category_and_macro_differences()

originality.positive: Combines controlled temporal, repetition, and positional probes with a prospective test of whether diagnostic findings guide useful model ablations under the existing compatibility contract.
originality.negative: Perturbation attribution, counterfactual recommendation explanations, and retraining controls are established; task integration alone is not a new explanatory principle.

future_potential.positive: A frozen, identified-user protocol could support reusable comparisons of recency, denoising, and scoring interventions across all four datasets.
future_potential.negative: Distribution shift, sparse recurrence, candidate dependence, and adaptive validation selection may limit its predictive value; evidence that the probes improve model selection is still required.

code_difficulty.positive: The initial diagnostic version reuses existing encoding and scoring hooks without retraining, pretrained weights, or new architecture dependencies.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable user manifests, prefix extraction, mask and position handling, distinct matched controls, missingness, and prospective ablation accounting require substantially more care than simple sequence deletion.

related_work.title: CETRec
contributions: The supplied research summary distinguishes absolute and relative temporal order and describes counterfactual tuning.
limitations: Temporal sensitivity alone does not establish recommendation usefulness, causal preferences, or the value of a particular architecture change.

related_work.title: Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns in Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Compares sequence-shuffling approaches and identifies item availability as a possible source of apparent sequential signal.
limitations: Preserving an item multiset during shuffling does not control all availability effects.

related_work.title: Semantically Consistent Contrastive Learning
contributions: Motivates caution when treating cropping, masking, and reordering as semantics-preserving operations.
limitations: Its augmentation motivation does not validate a particular intervention as a faithful explanation or useful training prescription.

related_work.title: On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies
contributions: Examines recommendation-evaluation reliability under different sampling strategies.
limitations: Fixed diagnostic candidates improve paired comparability but cannot establish full-catalog quality.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR
contributions: Addresses false-negative harm associated with hard-negative training.
limitations: Does not establish that lexical similarity or attribute disagreement supplies reliable negative relevance labels.

related_work.title: Original SASRec sampler
contributions: Provides the shifted sequence and next-item target construction underlying leakage-free prefix extraction.
limitations: The supplied task adapter remains authoritative for tuple structure, preprocessing, and user-identity availability.

related_work.title: SASRec PyTorch implementation
contributions: Illustrates absolute positional embeddings, causal masking, and final-feature scoring relevant to perturbation attribution.
limitations: The actual trained architecture must be checked; this reference does not guarantee identical masking or positional behavior.

related_work.title: CETD
contributions: The supplied summary describes sequential-history perturbations that consider temporal dependencies.
limitations: Explanation tests do not establish that sensitivity predicts improvements after changing and retraining SASRec.

related_work.title: ACCENT
contributions: Estimates historical-action influence for counterfactual recommendations.
limitations: Historical-action influence is distinct from evidence supporting an architecture prescription.

related_work.title: ROAR: A Benchmark for Interpretability Methods in Deep Neural Networks
contributions: Uses removal, retraining, and random-removal comparisons to evaluate attribution methods.
Motivates concern about distribution shift in inference-only removal tests.
limitations: Its methodology is a precedent rather than direct evidence that sequential-recommendation diagnostics predict useful architecture changes.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can reverse model ordering even in expectation.
limitations: Does not invalidate the pinned sampled benchmark as the specified selection target; it limits extrapolation to full-catalog quality.

related_work.title: The reusable holdout: Preserving validity in adaptive data analysis
contributions: Establishes risks from adaptive reuse of held-out data.
limitations: Freezing diagnostics and capping comparisons do not themselves provide the formal protections of a reusable-holdout mechanism.

related_work.title: Amazon Reviews 2023 benchmark scripts
contributions: Documents preprocessing that can retain only the earliest user–item interaction, eliminating exact-item recurrence.
limitations: Does not establish which deduplication transformation the pinned RecHarness pipeline uses; recurrence coverage must be measured from model-visible training histories.
